doc.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

title: Introverted players who avoided the scene
summary: Davey Schildkraut, Bill Trillia, Tony Frasella and Don Joseph as misfits.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: No. Because I have a feeling, no. And then there were other people, there was some musicians who almost craved anonymity, gifted, like Davey Schildkraut. You ever heard of him?

Well he was like this inside, and everybody, Stan Kenton was after him and I think he might have been with him for a minute and he quit. He just didn’t want to deal with all that. He wound up working in a post office and talking about aliens. And then there’s this terrific pianist, a friend of mine I haven’t seen in years who lives out in Jersey and he just teaches and plays in bars. His name is Bill Trillia. He plays on a Mingus record. There’s guys like that. And then there was this folk hero Tony Frasella, a little trumpet player, he’d carry his trumpet in a paper bag, and Don Joseph. These guys were like all little —
